provenance.note: the reese turned to its sine, for the fast broken beat's line as source 8's first tune plays it (read in memory, `notes/rounds/dnb-5.md`): a sine carrying the note, gliding into the next (`glide`) and wobbling its pitch on the eighths (`pitchCents`). Revision 2 (his ear on revision 1, 10-05: the bass all sub, where source 8's has a rounded body across the range): the recording's harmonics, each read against the floor between them, stand at -32 dB for the third and a level shelf of -41 to -48 from the fourth to the ninth (170-420 Hz), where revision 1's fell from -47 to -62; so the saws come up (0.12 to 0.2), high-passed off the second harmonic (`sawFloor` 3.6) under a resonant corner at the shelf's top (480 Hz, 10 dB) that hardly sweeps (0.2), and they all but stop drifting (`detune` 0.08 to 0.02): on notes a sixteenth to a beat long, three saws eight cents apart start in phase and cancel within a beat, so the body rang at the attack and fell 9-12 dB by 300 ms while the sine held, where the recording's body holds through the note. Its harmonics k3-k12 now stand within 3 dB of the recording's on the mean (revision 1: 9). Its loudness is the deep reese's until the voice gate measures it. Revisions 3-8 (the liquid bass rounds, 10-06/07, notes/rounds/liquid-v.md): an unequal pair — a second pure sine 6.59 Hz above the note at 0.33 of its level (subBeatHz, subBeatLevel), its phase kept on the theme's clock across runs (subBeatPhase) and its level a curve a note may write (subBeatCurve) — both sines on one audio-rate pitch signal, so their spacing holds through a bend; the third harmonic 0.10 and following the pair's phase and envelope (subBodyFollow); the old level LFO off (levelDepth 0, the trim 0.2 to 0.1787 to keep its mean level); an optional low entrance of its own (subEntryLevel, subEntryCents, subEntrySeconds; nought unless a note asks, and silent when a held note is resumed); and the dips back in 40 ms (dipRecovery). A note's bend and pair curve resume where a seek finds it held (curveDuration). The liquid knobs (10-07, the sound unchanged): V's numbers stand in the row's own parameters, each a desk line in a declared range, where they were the controls' defaults — the pair (pair.hz 6.59, pair.level 0.33), the third harmonic (subHarmonics[1] 0.10), the entrance's level, cents and seconds (entry: 0.5, 700, 0.18) and the dips' recovery (dipRecovery 0.04); a note may still write its own, and a pair curve or an entrance a note writes is heard scaled by the desk's move over the row's number (exactly one at rest).
